suppress.notes: SSE stream corruption with view fragments. This application exposes no Server-Sent Events endpoints: no SseEmitter, ServerSentEvent, or text/event-stream producer anywhere in src/main.

WebFlux + Aalto XML maxInMemorySize bypass. Requires WebFlux and the Aalto XML processor; this is a Spring MVC application (spring-boot-starter-web, no spring-boot-starter-webflux) and Aalto is not on the dependency tree.

Pre-flight header predicate bypass in WebFlux functional endpoints deployed on DispatcherServlet. No WebFlux on the classpath and no functional endpoints: zero RouterFunction/RouterFunctions usages. Routing is annotated controllers only.
Request headers exposed in a WebFlux WebSocket error path. No WebFlux and no WebSocket support is configured in this application.

User-supplied property paths through Spring's data binding infrastructure. This application does not use that infrastructure: zero occurrences of @ModelAttribute, @InitBinder, DataBinder, WebDataBinder or BeanWrapper in src/main. Request payloads arrive via @RequestBody (Jackson deserialisation) and @RequestParam/@PathVariable simple type conversion, none of which walk property paths.
SpEL safety guard bypass via SimpleEvaluationContext. This application evaluates no SpEL expressions: no SimpleEvaluationContext, ExpressionParser or SpelExpression usage in src/main.
SSE stream corruption via the functional web framework. Requires RouterFunction based routing and SSE; this application has neither.

WebAuthn user-verification bypass with a distributed HTTP session store. This application does not use WebAuthn or passkeys, and is stateless (SessionCreationPolicy.STATELESS) with JWT Bearer authentication -- there is no HTTP session store at all.

Spring Security's embedded UnboundID LDAP server registers an administrative credential and binds its listener broadly. This application uses no LDAP: no UnboundIdContainer, no spring-security-ldap dependency, and authentication is database-backed with JWT.

DOMPurify before 3.4.11 lets an uponSanitizeAttribute hook persist changes to the ALLOWED_ATTR allowlist across calls. It reaches us only as a transitive bundle inside the swagger-ui webjar that springdoc 2.8.17 ships; nothing in this project calls DOMPurify, and the React frontend does not depend on it (no dompurify entry in ui/package.json or ui/package-lock.json).
More to the point, the API documentation is not served in production at all: application-prod.yml sets springdoc.api-docs.enabled=false and springdoc.swagger-ui.enabled=false, so those paths return 404 and the vulnerable script is never delivered to a browser.
Note on the score: dependency-check displays 5.1 (CVSS v4.0) but failBuildOnCVSS compares the v3.1 score, which is 7.2 - which is why this fails the build despite appearing to sit under the threshold.
